title: Determining Protein and RNA Contribution to Condensate Organization in U-2 OS Cells
author: Parker, Parker
materials: This section describes how to seed and transfect U-2 OS cells with the fluorescent-tagged marker protein of interest. If a fluorescent protein was knocked in or otherwise expressed previously, transfection (Steps 3 and 4) can be skipped, and cells can be cultured normally before proceeding to Step 5 when they are at the desired confluency.1.Sterilize 12 mm round coverslips by submerging them in 70% ethanol.a.Allow the residual ethanol to evaporate before rinsing with PBS.Note: Other coverslip sizes work so long as they can be manipulated in the 24-well plate.2.Using sterile tweezers, rinse the coverslips in 1X PBS before moving the coverslips to the wells of a 24-well plate.3.Seed cells on coverslips at a density such that they will be approximately 70% confluent the next day for transfection.Note: Investigators should test the optimal seeding density for their specific transfection.4.After ∼16–24 h, transfect the plasmid encoding the fluorescently-tagged marker gene using the lipofectamine 3000 protocol: https://assets.thermofisher.com/TFS-Assets/LSG/manuals/lipofectamine3000_protocol.pdf.5.Allow transfection to proceed for 16–48 h in a cell culture incubator.Note: Seeding density and transfection duration can be modified to maximize transfection efficiency.Note: Transfection can induce stress granules.13 If working with stress granules, ensure that enough time has passed to allow transfection-induced stress granules to resolve.Note: Alternative transfection reagents and protocols can be used.Note: Refer to the manufacturer’s instructions for troubleshooting and optimizing transfection.

steps.title: Sterilize round coverslips
steps.instruction: Submerge 12 mm round coverslips in 70 % ethanol, let residual ethanol evaporate, then rinse briefly with 1X PBS.

steps.title: Place coverslips in 24‑well plate
steps.instruction: Using sterile tweezers, transfer the rinsed coverslips to individual wells of a 24‑well plate.

steps.title: Seed cells to 70 % confluence
steps.instruction: Seed U‑2 OS cells on the coverslips at a density that will reach ≈70 % confluence the next day (≈16–24 h later).

steps.title: Transfect fluorescent marker (if needed)
steps.instruction: If the cells do not already express a fluorescent reporter, transfect the appropriate plasmid (e.g., G3BP1‑GFP, GFP‑NPM1, or GFP‑Actin) using the Lipofectamine 3000 protocol; incubate 16–48 h in a cell‑culture incubator.

steps.title: Induce stress granules (optional)
steps.instruction: For stress‑granule experiments, add 500 µM sodium arsenite to the medium and incubate 1 h before any enzyme treatment.

steps.title: Permeabilize cells with Tween‑20
steps.instruction: Wash cells briefly with PBS, then incubate with 0.2 % Tween‑20 in appropriate buffer for the time specified for enzyme entry (typically a few minutes).

steps.title: Treat with degradative enzyme
steps.instruction: Add the chosen enzyme directly to the permeabilized cells:

substeps.instruction: Proteinase K: 0.02 U µL⁻¹ for 3 min at room temperature.
RNase A: 100 µg mL⁻¹ (≈100 µg µL⁻¹) and RNase I: 1 U µL⁻¹ for the same duration if RNA degradation is desired.

steps.title: Assemble coverslip sandwich
steps.instruction: Prepare a slide sandwich as follows:

substeps.instruction: Label the slide with sample identity.
Place a 24 × 30 mm rectangular coverslip in the middle of the slide, perpendicular to the slide surface.
Deposit 1 µL VECTASHIELD mounting medium in the center of the rectangular coverslip.
Using fine‑point tweezers, remove the round coverslip (with cells) from the wash solution and place it face‑down into the VECTASHIELD droplet.
Gently press the round coverslip to expel excess liquid (avoid lateral sliding).
Wick away remaining liquid with a torn Kimwipe.
Adhere a Grace Bio‑labs Silicone Isolator (catalog JTR20R‑0.5) to the center of the slide.
Place the coverslip sandwich so the round coverslip faces the slide and the rectangular coverslip faces outward, aligning the rectangular coverslip over the isolator.
Press the rectangular coverslip directly over the isolator to seal the sandwich.

steps.title: Image cells
steps.instruction: Image the prepared slides on the same day using an epifluorescent or confocal microscope (60× objective or higher recommended).

substeps.instruction: Set lamp/laser powers appropriate for the fluorescent proteins and FISH probes; keep settings identical across conditions.
Select cells with normal morphology (intact nuclei, visible cytoplasm, no obvious damage).
Acquire full‑depth z‑stacks of each cell of interest.
Save images in a format compatible with downstream FIJI/MATLAB analysis.

steps.title: Identify FISH spots with FISH‑quant
steps.instruction: Use the MATLAB implementation of FISH‑quant to detect individual smiFISH spots.

substeps.instruction: Download and install FISH‑quant (including Signal Processing Toolbox).
Place each channel in a subfolder named C# (e.g., C1).
Open FISH‑quant, adjust experimental parameters (pixel size xy, pixel size z, refractive index, NA, excitation wavelength, microscope).
Load the image, define cell outline, run detection, and set a detection threshold that yields a clear plateau on the spot‑number curve.
Apply the threshold to all cells and save detection settings.

steps.title: Deconvolve assemblies with Gaussian Mixture Model
steps.instruction: Run the provided GMM script to separate discrete spots from larger RNA assemblies.

substeps.instruction: Open WRAPPER_analyze_smFISH__EXP_v1.m in MATLAB (located in FISHquant/locFISH/).
Run the script, selecting the parent folder containing all FISH‑quant results.

steps.title: Generate ROI and organelle masks in FIJI
steps.instruction: Create coordinate ROI for spots and binary masks for the organelle of interest.

substeps.instruction: Convert GMM spot coordinates (Pos_X, Pos_Y) to µm by dividing by the pixel size (Pix‑XY) and save as a two‑column CSV (X, Y).
Open the corresponding max‑intensity projection in FIJI and import the CSV with the Spot_coordinate.ijm macro to create a multipoint ROI; save it.

For organelle masking, smooth the same projection (Process → Filters → Gaussian Blur) with an empirically chosen sigma, then Threshold (Image → Adjust → Threshold) using a consistent channel across control and treated samples.
Create a selection (Edit → Selection → Create Selection), add it to the ROI Manager, and save.

steps.title: Quantify spot‑mask overlap and plot
steps.instruction: Measure how many FISH spots fall within the organelle mask and visualize the results.

substeps.instruction: Open the raw (unsmoothed) image, make an unblurred max‑intensity projection, and load both the spot ROI and organelle mask ROI.
Run the Spot_overlap.ijm macro to obtain counts of total spots and spots inside the mask (output appears in the FIJI Log).
Save the results and plot the fractions using any preferred graphing software.

steps.title: Perform line‑scan intensity analysis (Analysis 2)
steps.instruction: Measure fluorescence intensity across assemblies using FIJI line profiles.

substeps.instruction: Open the image, create a max‑intensity projection, and select the straight line tool.
Draw a line that passes through the assembly and extends beyond it on both sides (e.g., 6 µm total length for stress granules).
Press ‘k’ to record the intensity profile, then save the data (Data → Save Data).
Repeat for multiple assemblies in multiple cells.
Align profiles by centering on the maximum intensity point, truncate to a fixed window (e.g., ±3 µm for stress granules), and average intensity at each distance.
Plot the averaged line profile (e.g., with ggplot2 in R).

steps.title: Measure average maximum intensities (Analysis 3)
steps.instruction: Determine mean peak intensities of discrete spots, RNA assemblies, and fluorescent organelles.

substeps.instruction: For discrete spots: open the max‑intensity projection, load the multipoint ROI generated in step 8, and use ROI Manager → Measure; save the Results table.

For assemblies and organelles: open the raw projection, load the binary mask ROI, split the selection into individual ROIs (ROI Manager → More → Split), delete any spurious ROIs, then Measure and save the Results table.
Determine background intensity by measuring three 1 µm² regions lacking signal in each channel; subtract the average background from all measured intensities.
Plot background‑subtracted average maximum intensities using preferred software (e.g., ggplot2 boxplots).

description: This protocol provides a workflow for testing the contribution of proteins and RNAs to the ultrastructural organization of RNP granules/membraneless organelles. Specifically, this protocol describes a process for introducing degradative enzymes, such as nucleases and proteases, to living U-2 OS cells using a low concentration Tween-20 permeabilization. Following the degradation of the cellular components of choice, the state of the organelle is examined using fluorescent reporter proteins and single-molecule (sm-) or single-molecule inexpensive Fluorescence In Situ Hybridization (smiFISH).2,3 This protocol was recently used to demonstrate that intermolecular RNA-RNA interactions contribute to the organization of stress granules.1 Similarly, this protocol was used to show that nucleolar structure is largely retained upon protein degradation.1 As this protocol has succeeded in both cytoplasmic and nuclear compartments, we anticipate it will be capable of discerning the structural role of proteins and RNAs in any intracellular membraneless organelle of interest. Before beginning the experiment, we obtained U-2 OS cells stably expressing G3BP1-GFP protein as a stress granule reporter or a vector for the transient expression of GFP-NPM1 or GFP-Actin to mark nucleoli and the actin cytoskeleton, respectively.4,5,6 Additionally, we ordered smFISH or smiFISH probes for resident stress granule (NORAD, PolyA) or nucleolar (snoRD3A, 47S-ETS1) RNAs. Investigators should use protein markers and RNA probes relevant to their organelle of interest, as discussed in more detail below. Furthermore, though we have only validated this protocol using U-2 OS cells, it is expected to work with any cell line that is sufficiently adherent to remain attached to coverslips following permeabilization and protease treatment.
